title: sre-weekly-update-2026-07-25
content:
SRE Weekly Update — 2026-07-25
Owner: Aisha Patel
Summary: light week overall; one production incident (partial degradation of streaming responses) escalated Friday morning with a targeted rollback and mitigations. Ongoing work: SLO tuning for hosted-api streaming, quota tiering rollout for dedicated pools, continued on-call rotation adjustments.

Highlights:
- Production incident on 2026-07-24 09:13 UTC impacting streaming responses for hosted-api in us-west1. Root cause: regression in streaming session management introduced in runtime PR #1284 that changed keep-alive handling for long lived SSE connections.
- Fix: rollback to runtime v2.13.1 at 09:42 UTC; mitigation included temporarily disabling experimental persistent-conn optimization. Full service restored by 09:55 UTC.
- Customer impact: ~2.6% of requests in us-west1 saw truncated streams or early EOF for sequences > 4k tokens. No data loss; all requests responded with either an error or truncated stream.
- Pager rotation: covered by on-call Alice -> handoff to Bob for weekend. Handoff doc updated with runbook link.

Incidents:
1) Incident SRE-4782 (2026-07-24 09:13 UTC) — Streaming truncation / early EOF
- Symptom: streaming clients reported early EOF and partial responses during generation; internal metrics showed increased connection resets and higher 5xx ratio on streaming route /v1/generate/stream.
- Timeline: first alerts 09:10; SEV2 declared 09:20; rollback decision 09:35; rollback deployed 09:42; verification complete 09:55; incident closed 10:05 after monitoring window.
- Root cause: change in keep-alive semantics in runtime PR #1284 that caused some LV connections to be treated as idle and closed prematurely in combination with our NLB TCP idle timeout.
- Postmortem TODOs:
  - Backfill automated integration test for long-lived SSE streams (JIRA SRE-4790).
  - Add synthetic traffic job to generate long-streams in canary env.
  - Revisit NLB idle timeout policy and align with runtime keep-alive defaults.
  - Add alert for sudden jump in connection resets for streaming routes.

SLO / Metrics:
- Current SLOs for hosted-api-generation: availability (successful non-error responses) 99.9% monthly, p99 latency target 1.1s for short requests, 99th-percentile streaming completion within configured timeouts.
- This week: availability in us-west1 for generation endpoints: 99.87% (slightly below SLO due to the incident). Overall global availability still within target thanks to routing fallback.
- Observability: added new dashboards showing connection reset counts by region + route; recommend adding a streaming-specific SLI that captures early EOF rate per model.

On-call handoffs and notes:
- Primary on-call: Alice Nguyen (week of 2026-07-20). Secondary: Marcus Chen.
- Handoff on 2026-07-24 17:30: noted the incident and mitigations; weekend handoff to Bob Turner (starting 2026-07-25).
- Action: update handoff checklist to include running the streaming smoke test and verifying NLB metrics. (see linked runbook: CONFLUENCE-6342-sre-dashboard)

Ongoing projects & work in progress:
- Quota tiering for dedicated pools: pilot with two customers next week. Action owners: Elena Rodriguez + platform-eng.
- SLO tuning for streaming: experimenting with p95 vs p99 alerting thresholds to reduce noise. Owner: Jon Morales.
- Autoscaler tuning: observed small oscillations in GPU allocation for dedicated pools during traffic spikes; PR with adjusted cooldown landed, monitoring in canary.

Action items (owners):
- SRE-4790 (Jon) — add long-lived streaming integration test, due 2026-08-05.
- Update NLB idle timeout recommendation in infra playbook (Marcus), due 2026-07-30.
- Add streaming early EOF SLI + alert (Aisha), due 2026-07-29.
- Follow up with runtime team on PR review guidance to flag connection/keep-alive changes (Elena), due 2026-07-28.

Notes & follow-ups:
- Quick wins: add a short synthetic job that runs every 10m in canary generating 10k token streams to catch regressions early.
- Longer-term: consider client SDK changes to better rehydrate streams and resume after transient truncation (product discussion needed).
- Retrospective: incident response was fast; rollback decision path worked well. Need to reduce MTTD by improving streaming-specific alerting.

Meeting requests / dependencies:
- Please sync with runtime team (weekly touchpoint) to review keep-alive semantics and SDK compatibility — propose agenda item for 2026-07-27 runtime-sync.
- Request infra to review NLB configuration across regions for idle timeouts and cross-check with cloud provider docs.

Appendix / links:
- Incident ticket: JIRA-SRE-4782
- Follow-up task: JIRA-SRE-4790
- Runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- Runbook / dashboards: CONFLUENCE-6342-sre-dashboard

Notes to self: add a short checklist item for on-call to run the streaming smoke test after any runtime deploy. Keep this doc updated after the retro on 2026-07-26.

-- end of update
